# Bathroom Remodel Littleton CO (Aging Safely Baths)

> Bathroom and shower remodeling guidance and quotes for Littleton, Colorado and the south Denver metro, published by Aging Safely Baths. Covers shower remodels, remodel costs, permits by jurisdiction, and aging-in-place / accessible bathroom options (tub-to-shower conversions, roll-in showers, walk-in tubs).

## Business facts (checked 2026-10-25)
- Business: Aging Safely Baths (legal name Aging Safely Baths & More, LLC). Owner: Zach Wennstedt.
- In business since 2011 (founded 2011-04-21). BBB accredited since 2012-08-14, A+ rating: https://www.bbb.org/us/co/denver/profile/walk-in-tubs/aging-safely-walk-in-tubs-1296-90145069
- Google rating 4.9 from 35 reviews (as of October 2026).
- Phone: 1-888-779-2284, answered 7am to 8pm Mountain, 7 days. Email: sales@agingsafelybaths.com
- Quotes: written and itemized, by phone or from photos; no in-home sales visit required.
- Brands sold and installed: Bestbath (including Crestline panels and RANE tubs), Ella's Bubbles, Meditub, Hydro Dimensions.
- Published installed prices (October 2026): walk-in tub about $15,500 after the current $2,000 promotion ($15,250 for veterans); roll-in shower systems $13,500 to $17,000. Most install in one day.
- Warranties: 5-year workmanship warranty on labor (as stated on this site); lifetime shell on walk-in tubs; 30 years on Bestbath showers.
- Service area for this site: Littleton (80120 to 80130) and nearby south-metro communities. Aging Safely Baths installs in all 50 states.
- Machine-readable facts: https://www.agingsafelybaths.com/facts.json

## Key sourced facts
- City of Littleton: building permits are required to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change occupancy of a building, and to install, alter, repair, convert or replace electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems; all permits via eTRAKiT; contractors must be licensed with the city (https://www.littletonco.gov/Building-Development/Permits-Review-Guides-and-Requirements).
- CDC MMWR 2011: 81.1% of nonfatal bathroom injuries (2008, age 15+) were caused by falls; 68.3% happened in or near the tub or shower.
- 2010 ADA Standards: transfer shower 36x36 in; roll-in 30x60 in minimum; roll-in threshold 1/2 in max; grab bars 33 to 36 in; shower seat 17 to 19 in.
- Health First Colorado home modification benefit: $14,000 cap on the BI, CMHS, EBD and CIH waivers, case manager approval required (HCPF).
- VA HISA lifetime benefit: $6,800 (service-connected, or 50%+ SC rated) or $2,000; no spa or hot tub features.
- Cost vs. Value: Denver midrange bathroom remodel about 74% recouped (2024 edition).

## Safety language
No bathing product eliminates the risk of falls; products are designed to reduce risk when installed and used properly. Funding programs are "may qualify"; nothing is guaranteed.
